instruction: Download all lecture PDFs for weeks 1-9 from the CS50 Python course page and save them to the lecture_slides folder.

metadata.explanation: Checks that at least 9 PDF files exist in /home/user/lecture_slides/ directory (lecture1.pdf through lecture9.pdf or similar naming). Verified by checking file count after filtering for .pdf extension.
metadata.verification: Evaluated by checking file existence and count in /home/user/lecture_slides/ directory via bash ls command.

llm_judge_reasons: Incorrect expected count: Instruction requires 'weeks 1-9' (9 PDFs) but evaluator expects min_files=10, which is semantically wrong
Metadata-implementation mismatch: Metadata says 'at least 9 PDF files' but actual min_files is set to 10
No content verification: Evaluator only checks count of PDF files, not whether they are actually CS50 lecture PDFs - would incorrectly pass if any 10 random PDFs were downloaded
Week numbering ambiguity: Config shows CS50 course starts at week 0, but instruction says 'weeks 1-9' - unclear if this means weeks 1-9 (9 files) or weeks 0-9 (10 files)
No filename validation: Cannot verify that downloaded files match expected lecture naming pattern (lecture1.pdf, lecture2.pdf, etc.)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Clarify instruction: If CS50 has weeks 0-9, instruction should say 'weeks 0-9' or 'all 10 weeks'. If it truly means weeks 1-9, set min_files=9
Update expected count: Change min_files to 9 if instruction means weeks 1-9, or to 10 if it means weeks 0-9
Add filename pattern validation: Check that files match expected naming (lecture0.pdf, lecture1.pdf, ..., lecture9.pdf or lecture1.pdf through lecture9.pdf)
Consider content verification: Optionally verify PDF file sizes are reasonable (not 0 bytes or corrupted downloads)
Fix metadata: Update explanation to match actual min_files value
